title: Anthropic shares cost less than GTA 6 after record IPO
excerpt: Anthropic shares fell below GTA 6's $79.99 price a week after its record IPO. The game made an estimated $3.79 billion in its first day on sale.
content_html:
'GTA 6' or an Anthropic share? You can get both for about $80.

By Georgia Hennessy

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-25T11:15:10.850Z

For about $80, you can spend a few hundred hours causing trouble in "GTA 6's" fictional recreation of Florida. Or you can buy a share of Anthropic and watch the trouble unfold on your brokerage app.

The choice got cheaper Wednesday morning. Anthropic stock dropped 9% in early trading, dropping below $75 per share as of around 9:45 a.m. ET, as the AI trade continues to unwind.

A standard copy of "Grand Theft Auto 6" costs $79.99 in the US.

It's a milestone for what you might call the "Granthropic benchmark." Morning Brew highlighted the comparison as the share price approached the game's price.

The two launches landed on November 19 and promptly set records. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO ever, pricing shares at $83.

The Claude maker opened at $111.50 and finished its first day at $97.17. After underwriters exercised an option to buy more shares, gross proceeds from the offering reached $93.5 billion.

"GTA 6" had an even more emphatic opening. Publisher Take-Two said it generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on day one, breaking the entertainment launch record. Its predecessor took three days to reach $1 billion when it came out in 2013.

The frenzy spread beyond consoles, with flight searches to Miami surging and merch reselling at huge markups.

Anthropic's day-one excitement has proved harder to sustain. As well as broader worries about the health of the AI trade, investors are questioning how the AI firm will translate demand for its products into lasting profits while paying for the computing power it requires.

Anyone who bought shares at the $83 IPO price is now underwater, less than a week after the record-breaking debut.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 players logged 683 million hours on PlayStation 5 in the game's first four days, according to Sony figures. Both debuts came roaring off the line.

So far, Vice City has held its speed better.
